claims.statement: A component prevented by an airway tube should be marked not testable with its interference recorded, without manufacturing a numeric total.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Separately recorded motor responses convey changes that a global summary score can conceal.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Early severe TBI with polytrauma requires urgent neurologic examination and cranial CT after life-threatening hemorrhage control.
claims.limitation: Consensus addresses early severe TBI with polytrauma. Applying its priority to a new unilateral deficit is clinical synthesis requiring review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Acute traumatic subdural hematoma thicker than 10 mm or producing more than 5 mm midline shift meets the surgical-evacuation criterion regardless of GCS.
claims.limitation: Older nonrandomized evidence. The constructed 12 mm measurement crosses the thickness criterion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: A life-threatening traumatic brain mass lesion warrants urgent neurosurgical intervention after systemic bleeding control.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Routine mild-head-injury decision rules should not exclude CT in adults taking an anticoagulant.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Routine repeat head imaging is unnecessary after a CT without hemorrhage in a neurologically baseline anticoagulated adult.
claims.limitation: New symptoms or neurologic deterioration require a new assessment. CDC implements ACEP 2023 and supplies one evidence lineage.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Anticoagulant use does not itself require admission after negative head CT when the examination is baseline and other admission indications are absent.
claims.limitation: Owner decision review.n3.head-injury-rule-scope-and-anticoagulant-exposure.v2 remains active. No anticoagulant resumption or withholding regimen is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Mild-head-injury discharge counseling includes delayed-hemorrhage warning symptoms and follow-up instructions.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Temporary circumferential pelvic stabilization centers compression at the greater-trochanter level.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Circumferential pelvic compression provides temporary early stabilization during hemorrhage resuscitation.
claims.limitation: One guideline lineage supports this point. Independent corroboration remains a review limitation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Pelvic arterial contrast extravasation can justify angiography and embolization after blood pressure improves.
claims.limitation: This concerns a resuscitated patient with an arterial target and supplies no universal sequence for uncontrolled shock.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Persistent pelvic hemorrhage with hemodynamic instability after angiography supports preperitoneal packing with pelvic stabilization.
claims.limitation: Packing and angiography are complementary. Source reassessment and center resources matter.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Neurologic findings after cervical trauma can require MRI despite CT showing no fracture or malalignment.
claims.limitation: One specialist recommendation set. CT-negative clearance does not apply to a new neurologic discrepancy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Progressive neurologic loss with continuing cervical cord compression supports early surgical decompression.
claims.limitation: No universal surgical-hour cutoff, steroid regimen or perfusion target is prescribed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: A cervical fracture extending into a transverse foramen is a high-risk pattern warranting CTA screening for blunt cerebrovascular injury.
claims.limitation: Evidence quality and population scope require clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Confirmed blunt cerebrovascular injury generally warrants antithrombotic treatment when bleeding risk permits.
claims.limitation: Several agents are reasonable. No aspirin-versus-heparin superiority or dose is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Routine stenting of grade II or III blunt cerebrovascular injury adds no established benefit to antithrombotic treatment.
claims.limitation: Selected progressive or symptomatic lesions can require intervention.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Repeat CTA near seven days can refute a provisional BCVI diagnosis and support treatment cessation when the initial finding was spasm or misinterpretation.
claims.limitation: Conditional low-quality evidence. Adequate repeat imaging and original-image review are necessary. Healing of a confirmed lesion is a different scenario.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Stable penetrating lower-extremity injury with abnormal vascular examination or ABI below 0.9 warrants vascular imaging.
claims.limitation: Evidence quality and population scope require clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: CTA is an appropriate primary vascular study when stable penetrating limb trauma requires imaging.
claims.limitation: Evidence quality and population scope require clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: An expanding hematoma supports operative exploration for arterial injury in an isolated penetrating limb wound.
claims.limitation: Associated skeletal or shotgun injuries can require localization imaging. The draft has neither.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: A reliable normal vascular examination and ABI greater than 0.9 can support discharge after isolated penetrating lower-limb trauma with follow-up.
claims.limitation: This excludes knee dislocation, high-energy blunt injury, unreliable examination and other admission needs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: An inadequately perfused limb needing fracture stabilization can receive a temporary vascular shunt before fixation and definitive vascular reconstruction.
claims.limitation: Low-quality evidence. Sequence depends on perfusion and injury. No fixed safe ischemia duration is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Palpable distal pulses do not exclude dangerous compartment-related tissue ischemia.
claims.limitation: Evidence quality and population scope require clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Increasing analgesic requirement, painful passive stretch and progressive tense swelling support acute compartment syndrome after limb injury.
claims.limitation: Evidence quality and population scope require clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Established acute leg compartment syndrome requires prompt complete compartment release.
claims.limitation: Military guidance supports completeness anatomy. Civilian drafts exclude late irreversible ischemia and prophylaxis thresholds.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Complete leg fasciotomy includes the deep posterior compartment, accessed by separating soleus attachment from the posterior tibia.
claims.limitation: Shared operative anatomy. Protected figures and procedural prose are excluded.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: For a high-risk civilian patient unable to report symptoms reliably, compartment pressure measurement can supplement repeated clinical assessment.
claims.limitation: JTS discourages routine measurements in the deployed environment. This is a monitored civilian hospital case. A single pressure is not a universal diagnosis.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: CT-based cervical clearance requires adequate high-quality imaging with coverage of the cervical spine.
claims.limitation: Applying the high-quality CT criterion to a documented incomplete acquisition is explicit synthesis. Repeat versus retrieval depends on actual acquisition coverage.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Under the EAST conditional protocol, a negative high-quality cervical CT can support collar removal in an obtunded adult blunt-trauma patient.
claims.limitation: Conditional very-low-quality evidence. The draft supplies protocol adoption and excludes a focal discrepancy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: MRI can depict selected traumatic axonal injuries that conventional CT may underdetect.
claims.limitation: This supports the modality distinction. The exact priority of repeat CT versus MRI for the constructed new focal change remains a carried clinical/source-review question.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with traumatic brain injury

claims.statement: Sedation can interfere with neurological response assessment; its administration and changes should be considered when interpreting a repeated examination.
claims.limitation: One originating scale resource supports this interference point. It does not establish that unchanged sedation excludes drug effect or replaces urgent evaluation of a focal change.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: A language barrier can make an orientation response uninterpretable; assessment in a language the person understands can resolve that barrier.
claims.limitation: One originating scale resource supports adaptation of communication. The constructed interpreter interview and collateral history, rather than language or demographic identity, establish the fictional patient’s baseline assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Aortic balloon occlusion has been proposed as a temporary hemorrhage-control bridge, rather than definitive pelvic source treatment.
claims.limitation: This describes the proposed purpose, not demonstrated benefit. Older WSES selection advice is qualified by the later UK in-hospital trial harm signal. No universal indication, zone, pressure cutoff or routine use is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: A cervical spinal cord injury can involve upper-limb function together with trunk or lower-limb sensation; preserved function below the injury can occur in incomplete injury.
claims.limitation: Basic NIH injury-level information and specialist consensus support this localization. The exact fictional examination is an applied clinical inference; no named syndrome or tract-level sensitivity is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Cervical traction reduction addresses selected displaced or locked-facet injuries; a progressive deficit from disc-related cord compression without a displaced joint presents a different mechanical treatment problem.
claims.limitation: One specialist recommendation set supports the locked-facet reduction role and surgery for progressive deficit. It is not a universal traction rule or a procedure-specific operative plan.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Steroid therapy does not mechanically remove a compressive disc lesion and should not replace decompression of a progressively deteriorating compressed spinal cord.
claims.limitation: One specialist recommendation set supports surgery with progressive compression and describes weak, conditional steroid evidence. No universal steroid prohibition, dose or timing recommendation is authored; the separate regimen/perfusion hold remains open.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: A pressure reading evaluates its sampled muscle compartment; it does not establish the state of separate unsampled compartments in an evolving injured leg.
claims.limitation: Applied inference from compartment-specific pressure assessment and four-compartment anatomy. Civilian pressure-adjunct reasoning comes from diagnostic reviews; combat prophylaxis recommendations are not transferred. No isolated diagnostic or operative threshold is adopted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: The UK-REBOA trial raised concern that adding the studied in-hospital balloon-occlusion strategy to standard care can worsen outcomes; routine benefit should not be presumed.
claims.limitation: One primary randomized trial lineage; its report and earlier journal publication are not independent corroboration. Restricted to the studied in-hospital strategy, without a numerical mortality claim or a universal prohibition in other settings.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: Cervical CT adequacy requires review of the necessary acquired anatomy; a truncated transferred reconstruction is different from an acquisition that never scanned those levels.
claims.limitation: The guideline supports CT adequacy before its conditional clearance recommendation. Retrieval rather than repeat exposure is an explicitly bounded author inference from the supplied complete source-acquisition record, not a guideline claim that inaccessible or inadequate images can always be recovered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

claims.statement: An ankle–brachial index places ankle systolic pressure over brachial systolic pressure; reversing numerator and denominator can change the trauma-screening classification.
claims.limitation: FEHES is used only for the stable basic ratio definition, not trauma management. EAST independently supplies the penetrating-extremity interpretation boundary. Both arms and both injured ankle arteries have equal constructed pressures, avoiding site-selection ambiguity.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the stated traumatic injury in an outside-hospital record

withheldDisagreements.point: Universal fasciotomy rule for delayed compartment syndrome with potentially nonviable tissue
withheldDisagreements.reason: Recommendations differ by tissue viability and deployed evacuation setting. No scored late-presentation key is emitted.

withheldDisagreements.point: Universal SCI steroid regimen and exact perfusion target
withheldDisagreements.reason: Older WFNS recommendations require a dedicated current comparison. No exact dose, duration or MAP target is emitted.

withheldDisagreements.point: Universal aspirin-versus-heparin ranking and mandatory stenting threshold
withheldDisagreements.reason: Sources do not establish a universal drug ranking or intervention threshold.

withheldDisagreements.point: Unique priority of packing over repeat angiography in persistent shock after a negative completion run
withheldDisagreements.reason: Clarified chronology still leaves missed or recurrent arterial bleeding credible. The revised candidate is unkeyed and parked for exact clinician adjudication.

withheldDisagreements.point: Routine REBOA benefit or universal rescue indication
withheldDisagreements.reason: Older bridge rationale and later primary trial harm signal cannot be collapsed into a universal indication. No scored REBOA key or universal efficacy claim is emitted.

rightsSummary: Complete attribution and links accompany independently written factual synthesis. Patient observations are fictional. No source excerpts, prose, tables, figures or algorithms are stored. Government status supplies no permission for third-party material.
researchScope: Targeted permitted-source survey across head injury, spine, BCVI, pelvis and limb trauma. Rankings are qualitative editorial judgments. No exam-frequency percentages or official testing weights are asserted.

accessLimitations.use: No facts from inaccessible content used.

accessLimitations.result: Publisher 429 and repository CAPTCHA prevented full retrieval.
accessLimitations.use: Candidate excluded from support. Search-result text was not used as a substitute.

accessLimitations.limitation: Full NIHR report, PMC 2024 landing page and general Bookshelf report endpoints failed or returned a browser check. The official NIHR scientific-summary PDF and its NCBI scientific-summary chapter were retrieved and their CC BY 4.0 notices verified.

revisionResearch.network: Permitted sources retrieved; specific full-report endpoints failed and are recorded. No inaccessible search snippet used as evidence.
